name: The Roelle furniture-finishing works, Mather Street

function.note: 'Used by the Roelle Furniture-finishing Company' (Andreas vol. 2, p. 717); Kraefft, Roelle & Co. are in Edwards 1871.

built.note: When it was built is not recorded.

research_note: THE ROELLE WORKS, built by T-3831 for the 1871 scene: 'Eleven feet south of the mills stood a three-story building, fifty by seventy feet, siding on Mather Street. This was used by the Roelle Furniture-finishing Company, and was filled with combustible materials' (Andreas vol. 2, p. 717). Some of the best steamers worked on it and on Bateham's property after ten, 'But in the very face of those efforts, the Roelle structure went up in smoke and flame.' No picture of it is known.

documented_range.note: Standing on the night of the fire, which destroyed it (Andreas vol. 2, pp. 406, 712-718).

position.symbolic_location: On the line of Mather Street, eleven feet south of Bateham's mills.
position.note: Eleven feet south of the mills, its long side on Mather Street's line (Andreas vol. 2, p. 717); where along Mather it stood is reconstructed. The footprint's origin is local E -195.0 N -1531.0.

derivation.reason: Laid out from the accounts' description of the block against the 1871 plan's streets; no traced frontage for the 1871 city is in data/traces/street_control.json to recompute it from.

footprint.note: Fifty by seventy feet, its long side on Mather Street (Andreas vol. 2, p. 717).

fire.note: 'In the very face of those efforts, the Roelle structure went up in smoke and flame' (Andreas vol. 2, p. 717), after ten and before the men were driven from the mills at half-past ten.
